question: What is the main goal of good nutrition in Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Replacing clinical treatments with herbal remedies
options.B: Preventing deficiency diseases and supporting optimal potential
options.C: Eliminating the need for agricultural market regulations
options.D: Reducing the cost of commercial food imports

explanation: You got this! In PHC, good nutrition is all about helping people stay healthy, avoiding illness, and reaching their full body and mind development. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why must community nurses look beyond the clinic when dealing with poor nutrition?

options.A: Because nutrition problems only exist inside large hospital wards
options.B: Because hospital management forbids nurses from talking about food
options.C: Because clinical medications can cure malnutrition completely on their own
options.D: Because root causes like poverty and food disruption require community-based action

explanation: Spot on! Nutritional challenges are often tied to bigger social and economic issues. Giving medicine alone isn't enough—we need community action and education too. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h1)

question: What do we call the main nutrients that give the body bulk energy and building blocks?
explanation: Great job! Macronutrients include carbs, proteins, and fats. They are the big players that supply your daily energy and physical structure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h2)

question: What does 'hidden hunger' mean in community nutrition?

options.A: Eating enough calories from starchy foods while lacking vital micronutrients
options.B: A sudden shortage of food caused by severe drought conditions
options.C: A psychological condition where patients refuse to eat despite starving
options.D: The physical sensation of hunger felt late at night

explanation: Exactly! Hidden hunger happens when someone gets enough food to fill their stomach (like heavy swallows of starch), but their diet misses the key vitamins and minerals they really need. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h2)

question: What is the main use of MUAC tape during community health outreaches?

options.A: To quickly screen for acute malnutrition using a simple tape
options.B: To determine the daily caloric intake of a household
options.C: To test blood sugar levels for diabetes screening
options.D: To calculate the exact body mass index of adult men

explanation: Well done! Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) uses color-coded tapes to quickly check if infants or young children are suffering from sudden, severe malnutrition. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h3)

question: A nurse notices more children losing weight in the months right before the new harvest. What activity helped spot this trend?
explanation: Spot on! Tracking how nutrition changes across different seasons helps nurses spot recurring health issues in the whole community before they get out of hand. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is a big plus of having homestead gardens in rural areas?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any community health education
options.B: Generating large profits on international export markets
options.C: Providing immediate access to fresh vegetables and fruits
options.D: Replacing local health clinics with herbal gardens

explanation: You got it! Homestead gardens mean families can just walk to their backyard to grab fresh, nutritious greens without needing extra cash or long travel. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h4)

question: Why is proper post-harvest management important for food security?

options.A: It increases the chemical fertilizer content in staple grains
options.B: It removes the need for farmers to rotate their crops
options.C: It forces farmers to sell all their crops immediately after harvesting
options.D: It prevents food loss from pests and spoilage during lean periods

explanation: Correct! Storing and preserving food properly keeps it safe from pests so families have something to eat even when crops are scarce. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h4)

question: What is the main focus of Behavioral Change Communication (BCC) in nutrition?

options.A: Addressing cultural habits and beliefs influencing food choices
options.B: Importing expensive nutritional supplements from abroad
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties for poor dietary habits
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests on food chemical safety

explanation: That's right! BCC looks past simple facts to understand the cultural and social reasons behind how people choose and prepare their meals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h5)

question: Why do nurses promote local foods during cooking demos instead of imported ones?

options.A: Local health policies legally forbid the use of foreign recipes
options.B: Local ingredients are usually more affordable and accessible to the community
options.C: Imported foods cause immediate illness in all age groups
options.D: Imported foods are always completely devoid of any nutritional value

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition teaching has to be practical. Using foods that families can easily buy or grow nearby ensures the habit sticks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h5)

question: Which deficiency condition is marked by severe muscle wasting and very little body fat?
explanation: You're doing great! Marasmus is a severe lack of energy and protein where a child looks extremely thin and wasted away because of absent body fat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary public health way to prevent iodine deficiency in a population?

options.C: Promoting the universal use of iodized salt

explanation: Correct! Iodized salt is the simplest, most effective way to reach everyone and stop conditions like goiter from developing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h6)

question: What does intersectoral collaboration mean when working on food security?

options.A: Working together across different fields like agriculture, health, and education
options.B: Relying solely on nursing staff to manage agricultural projects
options.C: Merging all hospitals into a single centralized government agency
options.D: Importing food supplies exclusively from neighboring countries

explanation: Spot on! Because food security involves farming, schooling, and healthcare, different ministries and sectors must join hands to fix it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h7)

question: Why is the agricultural sector so important when health workers try to improve nutrition?

options.A: Because farming practices have no impact on community health outcomes
options.B: Because farmers are legally required to diagnose nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Because agricultural workers manage all rural health clinics
options.D: Because agriculture determines how much and what types of food are produced

explanation: Brilliant! Farming dictates what food is available and how varied the food supply is, making agriculture the very foundation of good nutrition. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h7)
